answer: To resist sybil attacks, each agent identity must hold a non-transferable marble that seeds a memory-hard sequential proof. Every new attestation creates a fresh vertex in a dependency graph; the intermediate plume of state hashes must be recomputed live and cannot be reused or shared across clones. An attacker spawning n identities therefore incurs n separate memory footprints that scale linearly and cannot be amortized, raising the cost of a farm proportionally to its size.
